subject: Is it possible to have the page title in a Shiny app be a function of the host URL of the page?

messages.author: a5edeb4fa89b826c
messages.subject: Is it possible to have the page title in a Shiny app be a function of the host URL of the page?
parts:
It's interesting that for a fluidPage, the title, if left unspecified, defaults to the host URL of the page.  However, what I'd like to do is derive a page title *from* the host URL of the page, but not have it be exactly equal to the host URL.  

So, I guess the question is:  How can I access the host URL of the page outside of the shinyServer function which receives the session variable (which contains clientData and the url_* components)?  (Apparently "fluidPage" is able to do that somehow.)

messages.author: a5edeb4fa89b826c
messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to have the page title in a Shiny app be a function of the host URL of the page?
parts:
I read through the Shiny code and fluidPage (which calls bootstrapPage, etc.) doesn't seem to do anything to handle a NULL title.  It seems it's just regular behavior in browsers to have the window title default to the URL if the HTML document itself does not contain a title (which isn't strictly valid HTML I think).

Note that I also tried to see if head tag "hoisting" (as mentioned by Joe Cheng here: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/22 ) would work.  e.g.:
 tags$head( tags$title('A page by any other name would be as lame') )

I couldn't seem to get the title to be "hoisted".

Nevertheless, it still seems as though it's at least theoretically possible to modify the title of the generated HTML document from within the shinyServer function.

Any ideas?

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to have the page title in a Shiny app be a function of the host URL of the page?
parts:
Something like this?

ui <- function(req) {
  url <- paste0(req$rook.url_scheme, "://", req$HTTP_HOST,
    req$PATH_INFO, req$QUERY_STRING
  )
  fluidPage(title = toupper(url))
}

(Note that ui can be a function if you want, not just an object--if it's a function then the function is invoked each time the web page is served)

messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to have the page title in a Shiny app be a function of the host URL of the page?
parts:
My apologies.  I take that back about hoisting not working.  Actually, the title tag *is* hoisted into the head of the HTML document.  However, there is also an empty title (i.e. "<title></title>") that comes first.  Since the hoisted title comes *after* the empty title, the Chrome browser seems to give the empty title precedence over the second, hoisted title.

So close!

Any thoughts on either having a hoisted title get hoisted *above* the regularly-generated, empty title or having the hoisted title take the place of the empty title?

messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to have the page title in a Shiny app be a function of the host URL of the page?
parts:
That particular one is available at:
session$request$HTTP_USER_AGENT

Note that when running under Shiny Server/ShinyApps.io, not all HTTP headers are available this way, only ones that have been whitelisted by SockJS. This isn't an authoritative list but it will give you an idea:

https://github.com/sockjs/sockjs-node/blob/master/src/transport.coffee#L132-133
